hero.heading: I want to help good Christian groups go deeper.
hero.lead: Homeward grew out of more than thirty years of spiritual practice, leadership development, and a simple conviction: many Christian communities do not need another program. They need space to slow down, experience God together, listen deeply, and practice the way of Jesus in ways that carry into everyday life.
hero.question: What if the practices that help us become more present to God were easier to experience inside the groups we already have?
hero.support: That question is at the heart of Homeward.
hero.after_support: Rather than build a competing community, I want to come alongside existing Christian groups for a short season—helping people pray, reflect, listen, and grow together, then leaving the group with practices it can continue on its own.

questions.heading: Information matters. Formation takes practice.
paragraphs: I grew up in the Christian faith and have remained deeply drawn to Jesus, Scripture, prayer, service, and the conviction that faith should shape the way we actually live.
Over time I became increasingly interested in a practical question: what helps a person become more present, less reactive, more compassionate, more grounded in God, and more capable of love?

Teaching matters. Theology matters. But I have also learned that transformation usually requires practice—repeated ways of praying, listening, reflecting, and showing up differently with God and with one another.

search.heading: I have spent decades learning what helps people actually change.
paragraphs: For more than thirty years I have studied and practiced prayer, meditation, silence, Scripture, spiritual reflection, retreat, and contemplative formation. That has included Christian meditation, Centering Prayer, breath prayer, contemplative Scripture, extended retreat, and learning from experienced teachers and communities.

Along the way I also learned from contemplative teachers outside Christianity. I value what was useful without pretending every tradition teaches the same thing. Homeward itself is intentionally Jesus-centered and rooted in Christian spiritual formation.

return.eyebrow: WHAT I KEPT COMING BACK TO
return.heading: The life and way of Jesus remained the center.
paragraphs: Through years of study and practice, the person of Jesus remained the deepest center of my spiritual life. The more I explored presence, surrender, compassion, forgiveness, and love, the more I found myself returning to the Gospels and to the way Jesus actually lived with people.

The Christian contemplative tradition helped me discover that silence, meditation, and deep interior prayer do not have to sit outside Christianity. They are part of our own history and can help people experience faith rather than only discuss it.
That is the spirit behind Homeward: Jesus-centered, practice-based, open to honest questions, and oriented toward becoming more available to God and more loving toward other people.
return.book_title: Prayer that becomes a way of life
return.book_body: Practices such as Centering Prayer, breath prayer, contemplative Scripture, silence, and reflection can help move prayer from something we occasionally do into a way of becoming more receptive to God.
return.quote: The goal is not to escape ordinary life. It is to become more available to God and more capable of love within it.

missing.heading: Many churches already have community. What if we helped those communities practice?
paragraphs: Churches already have small groups, care teams, recovery communities, staff teams, and people who know and trust one another. I became less interested in asking people to join one more thing and more interested in serving the communities that are already there.

That is why Homeward now begins with short, experiential offerings: a four-week group experience and a three-session Sacred Listening workshop. We come in, facilitate the experience, help people try new practices together, and leave the group with tools it can continue using.

The goal is not to replace a pastor, a church, a small-group leader, or a theological tradition. It is to add a layer of formation that helps people slow down, listen more deeply, and carry their faith into ordinary life.
missing.signature: That is the work I want Homeward to do.

trust.eyebrow: WHY I FEEL PREPARED TO SERVE A GROUP
trust.heading: Spiritual formation. Leadership development. Real life.
trust.lead: If I am invited into someone else’s group, I believe trust matters. My background brings together spiritual formation, organizational leadership, coaching and facilitation, and the ordinary formation of marriage, parenting, work, and community.

cards.title: Spiritual formation
cards.body: More than thirty years of contemplative study, prayer, meditation, retreat, and practice; Religious Studies and Anthropology; and ongoing work with Centering Prayer, breath prayer, contemplative Scripture, silence, reflection, and Sacred Listening.

cards.title: Leadership & facilitation
cards.body: Twenty-five years of business leadership, with formation through Stagen, ACE Coaching, HeartMath certification, TED certification, and high-trust mastermind and forum practices informed by YPO and Vistage.

cards.title: Family & ordinary life
cards.body: Together with my wife, Lorraine, for twenty years and married for sixteen; father of two teenagers; and deeply shaped by the everyday work of marriage, parenting, friendship, responsibility, and leadership.

trust.founder_eyebrow: HOW I HOPE TO SHOW UP
trust.founder_heading: Prepared enough to lead. Humble enough to listen.
founder_paragraphs: I have spent much of my professional life building teams, developing leaders, facilitating difficult conversations, and trying to create cultures where people can be both honest and accountable.

The best groups I have experienced—spiritual, professional, and personal—share some of the same qualities: trust, confidentiality, curiosity, personal responsibility, good questions, and enough structure for real conversation to happen.

That is what I want to bring into Homeward: not expertise from above, but thoughtful facilitation that helps people experience something together and discover what is already emerging within the group.
trust.founder_quote: The point of my background is not to make Homeward about me. It is to help me serve your group well.
trust.summary: Homeward is Jesus-centered, experiential, and designed to strengthen existing Christian communities through guided practice, deeper listening, and honest conversation.
trust.disclaimer: The programs, certifications, organizations, teachers, and communities referenced here describe my personal formation and experience. Their inclusion does not imply formal sponsorship or endorsement of Homeward.

final.heading: Keep your group. Deepen the experience.
final.lead: If you lead a small group, care team, staff team, recovery community, or other Christian group and want to introduce contemplative practice in a grounded, approachable way, Homeward is designed to come alongside what you are already doing.

steps.title: Begin with four weeks.
steps.body: Give your existing group a guided taste of contemplative prayer, Centering Prayer, Sacred Listening, reflection, and everyday practice.

steps.title: Or focus on Sacred Listening.
steps.body: Use a three-session workshop to help people become more present, listen with compassion, and help others feel seen, heard, and loved.

steps.title: Keep what serves your people.
steps.body: Homeward steps back after the experience. Your group keeps its relationships, leadership, identity, and the practices that were useful.
